minutes.headline: Commission approved Lake Shirley herbicide spot treatments up to 40 acres; Sunset Lane treehouse and dock debate continued.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed a small town forest cutting plan, approved Lake Shirley treatments with a 40-acre cap, and heard several wetlands filings. Much of the meeting was a debate over a treehouse and docks at 338 Sunset Lane and whether landowner permission is needed for docks on town land. Enforcement matters, a tax title program and a stewardship grant were also discussed.

votes.motion: Approve the Lake Shirley treatment at the concentrations presented, allowing spot treatments up to a total of 40 acres, subject to the map
Approve 649 septic installation with standard conditions
Approve 141 Mill Street house with general conditions plus demarcation of limit of work in the 50-foot no-structure zone
Continue 12 Johnson Street hearing to June 7th at applicant request
Continue hearing with applicant permission so plan can be updated to show wall dimensions

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission moved to approve herbicide spot treatments at Lake Shirley, capped at a total area and subject to a map; the recording does not make the vote audible.
A septic installation at 649 was approved with standard conditions, and the vote passed.
A house at 141 Mill Street was moved for approval with general conditions and a marked limit of work; the vote is not audible in the recording.
Most of the meeting was debate over a treehouse and docks at 338 Sunset Lane and whether docks on town land need landowner permission; it ended with no resolution.
A retaining wall hearing was continued so the plan can show wall dimensions, and a contractor was to be invited to the June 21st meeting to review procedures.

why_it_matters: Lake Shirley treatments affect a town water body used for recreation, and the Sunset Lane debate bears on whether docks and structures near town land need permission, a question that could apply to other waterfront owners.
A tax title collection program using an outside agency was discussed, and its interest charges could fall on owners behind on property taxes.
